description: Domain-neutral graph-native adaptive control. Verified outcome receipts produce signed temporal-difference errors and bounded eligibility credit across recent state, action, controller, and attention choices. Expected noise, volatility, and model ignorance remain distinct and independently shape precision, plasticity, and exploration. Applied motor commands author efference copies and predicted sensory consequences; receipt-backed residuals calibrate a learned forward model. Repeated reliable action sequences become option candidates. Interoceptive forecasts expose allostatic errors, and a conservative TTL-bounded competition broadcasts selected graph content to held consumers. The broadcast is functional routing only and makes no claim about consciousness.

rules.name: adaptive_control_mint_controller_value
rules.comment: A controller gets one graph-held value estimate on first use. The estimate belongs to that controller, not to a global scalar critic.

rules.name: adaptive_control_attach_controller_value
rules.comment: Later decisions by the same controller reuse its held estimate.

rules.name: adaptive_control_predict_outcome
rules.comment: The controller-specific value estimate becomes an explicit prediction with predicted provenance. It is not an observation.

rules.name: adaptive_control_open_bounded_eligibility_trace
rules.comment: A committed decision captures the state, action, controller, and attention choices that may deserve later credit. Expiry is an explicit epoch bound.

rules.name: adaptive_control_author_sensorimotor_prediction
rules.comment: An intended command creates an efference copy and a predicted sensory consequence in parallel. Neither is evidence that the world applied the action.

rules.name: adaptive_control_compute_signed_prediction_error
rules.comment: Only a verified outcome receipt closes a prediction. TD error is observed value plus discounted next estimate minus the prior prediction. Noise, volatility, and ignorance stay separate.

rules.name: adaptive_control_assign_discounted_credit
rules.comment: Every still-eligible decision in the same context receives discounted signed credit once per outcome. The trace carries the four chosen components and controller values update locally.

rules.name: adaptive_control_expire_eligibility_trace
rules.comment: Clock evidence closes traces at their explicit horizon; fixed-point ticks do not age them.

rules.name: adaptive_control_calibrate_forward_model
rules.comment: Only a causal receipt permits an observed consequence to calibrate the forward model. Residual is observation minus prediction; self-attribution remains receipt-backed.

rules.name: adaptive_control_mark_reliable_decision
rules.comment: A decision is reliable only when both its sensorimotor residual and its value-prediction error are small.

rules.name: adaptive_control_propose_repeated_skill_option
rules.comment: Two temporally separate reliable executions of the same two-action identity sequence are evidence for a reusable option candidate. It is proposed, not silently adopted.

rules.name: adaptive_control_forecast_allostatic_error
rules.comment: Forecast demand before threshold failure. The allostatic error is desired reserve minus forecast reserve, with precision kept explicit.

rules.name: adaptive_control_offer_allostatic_broadcast
rules.comment: A sufficiently large predicted internal deficit competes for routing; it is not granted broadcast by fiat.

rules.name: adaptive_control_score_broadcast_candidate
rules.comment: Candidates compete on urgency plus precision-weighted salience. Expected imprecision cannot masquerade as priority.

rules.name: adaptive_control_refuse_exact_broadcast_tie
rules.comment: An exact top-score tie first mints an epoch-scoped refusal. Winner selection is gated by its absence, so a later fixed-point pass cannot accidentally break the tie.

rules.name: adaptive_control_mark_tied_broadcast_candidates
rules.comment: All candidates in the refused epoch are terminally marked; none can become a winner after peers are marked.

rules.name: adaptive_control_select_functional_broadcast
rules.comment: A unique sufficiently important winner becomes a short-lived routing episode. This is shared access among graph consumers, not a consciousness assertion.

rules.name: adaptive_control_deliver_functional_broadcast
rules.comment: Every graph-held consumer receives an availability edge to the same selected episode; consumers decide locally whether to use it.

rules.name: adaptive_control_expire_broadcast_candidate
rules.comment: Unselected candidates have the same explicit clock-bounded lifetime as winners; fixed-point ticks alone cannot age them.

rules.name: adaptive_control_expire_functional_broadcast
rules.comment: Clock evidence expires shared availability at the held TTL. Re-ticking without a later clock cannot consume time.

rules.name: adaptive_control_prune_expired_broadcast
rules.comment: An expired routing episode remains inspectable for a bounded retention interval, then only the transient episode is deleted.

rules.name: adaptive_control_prune_terminal_broadcast_candidate
rules.comment: Selected, expired, and tie-refused candidates are terminal evidence envelopes. Content nodes and any durable knowledge they reference survive.

rules.name: adaptive_control_prune_broadcast_tie
rules.comment: The epoch-scoped tie refusal is retained through its broadcast window plus the audit interval, then removed.

rules.name: adaptive_control_prune_expired_eligibility_trace
rules.comment: Expired traces are short-lived causal bookkeeping. Controller values and forward models learned through them are deliberately untouched.

rules.name: adaptive_control_prune_integrated_prediction_error
rules.comment: A prediction error integrated into its durable model has a bounded audit life. The learned transition/controller model survives deletion of the residual.
